answers: 열이 나요. 감기약 주세요. (열이 있어요. 감기약 주세요.)
증상: 콧물, 기침 / 약: 소화제, 연고
exercises: Fill in the blank with one word from the list (두통 / 배탈 / 콧물): 머리가 너무 아파요. ____이 있어요.
Fill in the blank with the right medicine: 손가락을 조금 베었어요. 상처에 붙이게 ____ 주세요.
Choose the correct particle in each blank (이 / 가): 기침( ) 나요. 그리고 콧물( ) 나요.
Translate into Korean with two short sentences: "I have a fever. Please give me cold medicine."
Complete the conversation with one word. 약사: 어디가 아프세요? / 손님: 어제 상한 우유를 마시고 ____이 났어요.
Sort these four words into two groups, symptoms (증상) and medicines (약): 콧물, 소화제, 기침, 연고
objective: Learners can tell a pharmacist their symptom with 10 core pharmacy words in short sentences such as '두통이 있어요' or '열이 나요', and ask for the right medicine with '○○ 주세요'.
summary: This worksheet teaches 10 core words for a Korean pharmacy: 5 symptoms (두통, 열, 기침, 콧물, 배탈) and 5 kinds of medicine (감기약, 소화제, 진통제, 연고, 밴드). Each word comes with one short, natural sentence. You then use the words in simple patterns: '○○이/가 있어요' or '○○이/가 나요' to say what is wrong, and '○○ 주세요' to ask for medicine. Note: Koreans usually say 열이 나요 (not only 열이 있어요), and 기침·콧물 also go with 나요. For an upset stomach, say 배탈이 났어요.
